# 1 Clement Chapter 18 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 18

**18:1** But what shall we say of David, who received attestation, and of whom God said: "I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, whom I have anointed with my eternal mercy"? [Ps 89:20; 1 Sam 13:14]

**18:2** But he himself says to God: "Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy; and according to the abundance of your compassion blot out my transgression.

**18:3** Wash me yet more thoroughly from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know my transgression, and my sin is before me continually.

**18:4** Against you alone have I sinned and done what is evil before you; so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.

**18:5** For behold, I was conceived in iniquity, and in sin my mother bore me.

**18:6** For behold, you have loved truth; the hidden and secret things of your wisdom you have made known to me.

**18:7** You shall purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; you shall wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

**18:8** You shall make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

**18:9** Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

**18:10** Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

**18:11** Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your holy spirit from me.

**18:12** Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.

**18:13** I will teach transgressors your ways, and ungodly men shall return to you.

**18:14** Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation; my tongue shall sing aloud of your righteousness.

**18:15** O Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth shall show forth your praise.

**18:16** For if you had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with burnt offerings you will not be pleased.

**18:17** The sacrifice of God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart God will not despise." [Ps 51:1-17 LXX]

---

*LOGOS formal equivalence. The LXX Ps 51 is one of the most quoted psalms in the early church.*
